query: We are investigating a specific eutectic high entropy alloy (comprising Al, Co, Cr, Fe, Ni) that exhibits a dual-phase lamellar structure and suffers from catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility. The operating regime is room temperature uniaxial tension. Known failures include the strength-ductility trade-off and stress concentration at phase interfaces. Design constraints require maintaining the alloy composition while altering the microstructure to arrest interfacial cracking and promote uniform plasticity. Propose a high-intensity thermomechanical treatment hypothesis that could transform the lamellar structure into a patterned configuration, explain the predicted boundary conditions for success (e.g., specific temperature/pressure windows), and define a falsification experiment involving conventional hot isostatic pressing to isolate the effect of extreme pressure.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high-intensity thermomechanical treatment involving severe plastic deformation (SPD) followed by a controlled, low-temperature annealing step will transform the coarse lamellar structure of the AlCoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy into a patterned, ultrafine lamellar configuration with coherent interfaces, thereby arresting interfacial cracking and promoting uniform plasticity at room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) with a coarse lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure (inter-lamellar spacing ~2 μm) exhibiting catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility under room temperature uniaxial tension.
generation.intervention: Severe cold rolling (e.g., >75% thickness reduction) at room temperature to induce high dislocation density and refine the lamellar spacing, followed by a short-duration annealing step (e.g., 900 °C for 5 min) to stabilize the refined structure without coarsening, creating a patterned ultrafine lamellar configuration.
generation.conditions: Room temperature for deformation; annealing temperature window between 650 °C and 900 °C (based on stepwise thermo-mechanical precedents) to ensure precipitate stability and interface coherence; strain rate ~10⁻³ s⁻¹ during tensile testing.
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine lamellar boundaries (target width <100 nm) and coherent precipitate interfaces (similar to δ-lamellae and γ″ particles in refractory HEAs) that facilitate dislocation transmission and shear rather than crack initiation.
generation.mechanism: The high-intensity deformation reduces the inter-lamellar spacing to a scale where dislocations are stored and pinned by alternating soft (fcc) and hard (B2) phases, similar to the strain-hardening mechanism in EHEAs. The subsequent annealing promotes the formation of coherent interfaces (as seen in stepwise precipitate systems) that relieve stress concentrations at phase boundaries, preventing the premature crack initiation observed in coarse lamellar structures.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant increase in ultimate tensile strength (targeting >1.2 GPa) while maintaining or improving ductility (elongation >15%) at room temperature, with a shift from interfacial cracking to uniform plastic deformation and high strain-hardening rates.
generation.baseline: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi EHEA with ~2 μm lamellar spacing, exhibiting a fracture stress of ~944 MPa and elongation of ~25.6% (or lower if brittle phases dominate), with failure dominated by stress concentration at phase interfaces.
generation.boundary: Success is bounded by the annealing temperature; exceeding ~900 °C may cause coarsening of the lamellar structure or dissolution of coherent precipitates, reverting to brittle behavior, while insufficient deformation (<50% reduction) may fail to refine the spacing enough to arrest cracking.
generation.uncertainty: The specific temperature window for the annealing step to achieve optimal coherence without coarsening is not explicitly defined for the AlCoCrFeNi system in the provided evidence, as the stepwise thermo-mechanical data comes from a different refractory HEA system (W-Ni-Fe-Ta). The exact mechanism of crack arrest in the AlCoCrFeNi system under extreme pressure is also not directly verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare AlCoCrFeNi specimens subjected to the proposed high-intensity thermomechanical treatment (75% cold rolling + 900 °C/5 min anneal) and compare them against a control group processed via conventional Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) at 1230 °C and 152 MPa (as per PMC5578249) without the severe plastic deformation step. Both groups will be tested under room temperature uniaxial tension.
measurements: Fracture surface morphology (SEM) to identify crack initiation sites
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HIP-only group (control) exhibits significantly higher ductility or reduced interfacial cracking compared to the thermomechanically treated group, or if the thermomechanically treated group shows no improvement in ductility (elongation <10%) and retains interfacial cracking, the hypothesis that high-intensity thermomechanical treatment transforms the structure to arrest cracking is falsified.
